section_1.title: The Intuitive Hook: The Cocktail Party Effect
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of 'selective focus'. Just as humans filter out background noise to listen to one speaker, models need to filter relevant tokens from a sequence.
section_1.example: Imagine a crowded party. You ignore the background chatter but immediately 'attend' to your name being called across the room.

section_2.title: The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values
section_2.content: Explain the Q, K, and V vectors using a database analogy. Define Q (what I'm looking for), K (what I have to offer), and V (the content I provide). Pre-requisite: Dot product as a measure of similarity.
section_2.example: A library search: Your search term is the 'Query'. The book labels are the 'Keys'. The information inside the book is the 'Value'.

section_3.title: Visualizing Attention Scores (Softmax)
section_3.content: Explain how the dot product of Q and K determines relevance. Use a heatmap animation to show how high-relevance tokens get 'bright' and low-relevance ones fade.
section_3.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired', the word 'it' has a high attention score (bright connection) to 'animal' but a low score to 'street'.

section_4.title: The Mathematical Workflow
section_4.content: Synthesize the components into the formula: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(dk))V. Visualize this as a weighted sum of values, where weights are determined by the alignment between Q and K.
section_4.example: Think of it as a weighted recipe: The Query decides the importance of each ingredient (Key), and we mix the flavors (Values) based on those importance weights.

section_5.title: Summary: Why Transformers Rule
section_5.content: Conclude by highlighting 'Parallelization'. Unlike RNNs that read one word at a time, Attention processes all words simultaneously, allowing for the massive scale of modern LLMs.
section_5.example: An RNN is like reading a book through a pinhole; a Transformer is like taking a high-speed photograph of the entire page at once.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Intuitive Hook: The Cocktail Party Effect", 
                          ["Transformers use selective focus like a party.", 
                           "Humans filter noise to hear one speaker.", 
                           "Models filter relevant tokens from a sequence."])

        # Animation Setup
        # Create representation of people talking
        people = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE).add(Dot(radius=0.05)) for _ in range(6)])
        for i, p in enumerate(people):
            self.place_at_grid(p, ["B2", "B4", "C3", "D2", "D4", "E3"][i])
        
        focus_person = Circle(radius=0.4, color=YELLOW).add(Dot(radius=0.08, color=YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(focus_person, "C5")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        self.play(FadeIn(people), FadeIn(focus_person))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_opacity(1)
        # Simulate background noise
        noise_waves = VGroup(*[Arc(radius=0.4, angle=PI/2, color=BLUE_D).move_to(p.get_center()) for p in people])
        self.play(Create(noise_waves), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_opacity(1)
        # Highlight focus and fade noise
        self.play(
            FadeOut(noise_waves),
            focus_person.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            people.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)
